origin.description: Locate the first word in each string.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, or an object coerced to character.

arguments.name: locale
arguments.text: NULL or "" for the default locale, or one locale identifier.

arguments.name: get_length
arguments.text: TRUE makes the second column the length. A miss on a real string is then -1.

origin.details: Equivalent to stri_locate_first_boundaries with type word and skip_word_none TRUE.
origin.value: An integer matrix with columns start and end, or start and length.
origin.example:
loc <- stri_locate_first_words("ab cd")
cat(paste0('stri_locate_first_words("ab cd") starts at ', loc[1, 1], '.\n'))

translation.description: Locate the first word in each string.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those. None is an empty vector.

arguments.name: locale
arguments.text: None or "" for the default locale, or one locale identifier.

arguments.name: get_length
arguments.text: True makes the second column the length. A miss on a real string is then -1.

translation.details: Calls stri_locate_first_boundaries with type word and skip_word_none true.
translation.value: A list of rows. Each row is [start, end] or [start, length].
translation.example:
from stringi.boundary import stri_locate_first_words
loc = stri_locate_first_words("ab cd")
print(f'stri_locate_first_words("ab cd") starts at {loc[0][0]}.')
